label: copy-phase re-input of digit 3 (from recall position 3 on)
explanation: Fires only during the copy phase, on steps where the fed-back input token is the digit 3 (essentially 100% of activation mass is on in_tok == 3 with phase == 2). It never fires on 3 in the original phase, on the delimiter, or on any other input token (5 stray weak activations on g). The bare condition (copy phase, input 3) has recall ~1.0 but precision 0.51; it is silent at recall_idx 0-1, weak/rare at recall_idx 2, and fires on ~25% of eligible steps from recall_idx 3 on, so the reported predicate requires recall_idx >= 3 (dev F1 0.80, mass recall 0.94). Within copy-phase 3 inputs, firing probability and magnitude are graded by the token being output next (the original token that followed the 3): highest when out_tok is g, p, 2, o, 3, r (precision 0.85-0.96, largest share of mass and top examples are mostly 3 -> p/g), lowest for c, v, w, d, e (precision 0.2-0.37). Rate also rises with the number of digits in the sequence. Excluding the low out_tok set barely changes F1, so it is described as modulation rather than part of the predicate.

issues: The core claim holds. All activation mass is in phase 2 (copy), in_tok==3 carries mass share 1.000, there are only 5 stray activations on g, and nothing fires in the original phase or on the delimiter. Copy phase plus input 3 alone gives precision 0.510, recall 0.9999 and mass recall 0.99996. The original predicate reproduces on test: P 0.723, R 0.904, F1 0.803, mass recall 0.936.

One stated fact is wrong. The explanation says the feature 'fires on roughly 25% of eligible steps from recall_idx 3 on'. In fact, among copy-phase inputs of 3 with recall_idx>=3 it fires on about 72% (dev precision 0.725). The 2.5% figure in the profile's by-recall_idx table is the rate over all copy steps, not over eligible steps.

The recall_idx cutoff is soft, not a hard boundary. At recall_idx==2 (the 3 was original token 1), copy-phase 3 inputs fire 27% of the time (P 0.269), and 57% of the time when the output token is a high-precision one (gpor23bil). At recall_idx==1 the feature is truly silent (P 0.0). 'Weak and rare at recall_idx 2' understates this.

The output-token modulation is broader and stronger than described, and it is the main source of systematic false positives. Within the predicate, precision by out_tok runs from v 0.25, w 0.33, c 0.36, d 0.47, e 0.47 through n/s/x/y 0.55-0.58 and m/0/1/a 0.64-0.70, up to g 0.99, p 0.99, 2 0.96, r 0.96, o 0.95, 3 0.94, b/i 0.90. It is a graded dependence on the original token that followed the 3, not a short list of exceptions. The test false positives shown are mostly of this kind (outputs e, a, w, s, y, z).

The other slices barely move precision (about 0.70-0.74): n_digits 1 vs >=2, in_count 1 vs >=2, prev_tok a digit, L>=8. Precision is lower on the last step (to_go==0: 0.64) and for L<=5 (0.63). Apart from out_tok, the remaining false positives look diffuse and threshold-like.

Better predicate: drop the low-precision outputs cdevw at recall_idx>=3 and add recall_idx==2 for high-precision outputs. This gives test P 0.771, R 0.888, F1 0.825, mass recall 0.941, against 0.803 for the original. The gain is real but modest, so the original label is approximately right but imprecise.
skeptic.revised_label: copy-phase re-input of digit 3 (mostly from recall position 3 on, fires on ~72% of such steps; strength graded by the original token following the 3: high for g/p/r/o/2/3, low for v/w/c/d/e)
skeptic.better_predicate: (phase == 2) & (in_tok == tok('3')) & (((recall_idx>=3) & ~isin(out_tok,[tok(x) for x in 'cdevw'])) | ((recall_idx==2) & isin(out_tok,[tok(x) for x in 'gpor23bil'])))

final_label: copy-phase re-input of digit 3 (mostly from recall position 3 on, fires on ~72% of such steps; strength graded by the original token following the 3: high for g/p/r/o/2/3, low for v/w/c/d/e)
